inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances. Dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house [...]
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has reaffirmed an essential limit on state power: serious accusations and failure to recover stolen articles alone cannot justify cancelling pre-arrest bail. Justice Sumeet Goel said there must be clear proof that liberty was misused or circumstances changed. That matters because pretrial detention can punish people before guilt is established, and its costs fall most heavily on those with the fewest resources. A fair justice system must protect due process rather than let the severity of an allegation substitute for evidence.
